pages.title: The Ahî Organization
pages.content:
The Ahî Organization was a religious and social institution. It first appeared in Anatolia in the 13th century and later played a significant role in the founding of the Ottoman Empire. Throughout the centuries, this institution guided society with rules for moral, social, and commercial life. The word ‘Ahî’ may come from two possible roots: either from the Old Turkish word ‘akı’, which means ‘generous and brave’, or from the Arabic word ‘ah’, which means ‘brother’ and highlights the idea of a brotherhood.

To clearly understand the role of the Ahî organization, we must first look at the Fütüvvet tradition, which deeply affected how Ahîs started in Anatolia.

vocabulary.definition: A large organization with an important role.

pages.title: The Fütüvvet Tradition
pages.content:
Fütüvvet is a social concept that started during the first century of Islam. It comes from the word ‘fetâ’ from the pre-Islamic period. In early Arab society, ‘fetâ’ described good qualities like generosity, bravery, and helping others. By the 9th century, this idea turned into an organized movement for young people. It helped them connect socially, economically, and politically. Also in the 9th century, as the Sufi movement developed from a personal lifestyle into an organized form, Fütüvvet took on a ‘Sufi Fütüvvet’ identity. Later, during the Abbasid period in the late 12th and early 13th centuries, it turned into an official organization. In its final stage, it joined together with the worker and artisan class. It began to work like a professional business group, but it still kept most of its Sufi spirit.

The idea of Fütüvvet reached Anatolia through the Abbasids. Starting in the 13th century, it developed its own meaning among the Anatolian Turks and became the Ahî movement.

vocabulary.definition: Good parts of a person’s character.
People who make things by hand.
The main feeling or character of something.

pages.title: The Caliph’s Robe
pages.content:
In fact, during the rule of Sultan Alâeddin Keykubad I (1220–1237), the Abbasid Caliph Nâsır-Lidînillâh (1180–1225) sent a Fütüvvet robe to the sultan. The Caliph saw himself as the leader of the Fütüvvet order, so he sent this gift through a special messenger. This messenger was Şehâbeddin es-Sühreverdî (d. 1234). Caliph Nasir wanted to rule the whole Islamic world, both in theory and in practice. Sühreverdî was his key advisor for this goal. Sühreverdî was a well-known mufassir, a hadith scholar, and a beloved Sufi. Because of this, he had the influence to bring different Fütüvvet groups together and organize them for this purpose.

To do this, the Caliph wanted to grant official status to the Fütüvvet institution, which was previously unofficial. By establishing it as a government institution, he wanted to give it power and get its political support. As a result, this group, which was independent for a long time when central governments were weak, would now be under state control. While doing this important task, the Caliph trusted Sühreverdî a lot, using his strong spiritual power and strategic ideas. When Sühreverdî arrived in Konya, people welcomed him with a great ceremony. He dressed Alaeddin Keykubad in the special robe sent by the Caliph. With this act, the Abbasid Caliph officially accepted Keykubad’s political power.

Greeted someone in a friendly way.

pages.title: Ahî Evran and the Spread of the Ahîs
pages.content:
Meanwhile, Ahî Evran, who played a key role in establishing the Ahî movement in Anatolia, also gained the support of the Seljuk sultans. Ahî Evran was a Sufi philosopher and scholar who traveled from Central Asia to Anatolia. He stayed in Denizli, Konya, and Kayseri for a time, and visited many other cities and towns before finally settling in Kırşehir. Known as the spiritual leader of leather workers and other craftsmen, Ahî Evran founded a zaviye in Kırşehir that became the socio-religious and professional center for artisans all across Anatolia.

The members of this organization spread quickly all across Anatolia. The movement spread from major cities to small villages, reaching both people in towns and nomadic people. In 13th-century Anatolia, the government became very weak. During this time, the Ahîs played an important role in city life, both in business and in politics. They showed their political and military power when the central government failed and there was no law or order. In fact, during the Mongol invasion, Ahî groups took control of city governments as local leaders.

The Ahîs opposed Gıyâseddin II. They suspected him of the death of Alaeddin Keykubad I. Keykubad I had supported the Ahî order. It is believed that he was poisoned by his son. Later, after the Mongols defeated Gıyâseddin II at Kösedağ, the Ahîs bravely helped defend Kayseri against the invaders, although the city finally fell.

pages.title: Values and Way of Life
pages.content:
Based on Islamic-Sufi ideas and Fütüvvet rules, the Ahî Organization had strong connections to tekkes and zaviyes. It also shaped business life by organizing the relations between masters, experienced workers, and young apprentices in their workshops. For example, during the Anatolian Seljuk period, this institution worked like a system of artisan organizations. In this role, it solved trade problems and managed relations with the state. Additionally, checking the quality of goods and setting the prices were among the main duties of the organization.

Their values, beliefs, and way of life from the 13th to the 16th centuries were written down in the Fütüvvetnâmeler (the guidebooks of the organization). Through these texts, Ahî traditions shared a deep connection with the cultural education of the Alevi-Bektashi community and other groups in Anatolia.

The Fütüvvet way of life has a few important rules that guide a person’s behavior. Followers are expected to be generous, honest, and thankful. They should always have a smiling face and speak with kind words. They must help their families, treat workers well, and share food with others. Also, it is very important to stay away from bad friends and spend time with wise elders instead. Finally, followers must avoid behaviors forbidden by the Qur’an and the Sunnah, such as drinking alcohol, and remember that this world is not permanent. They should also support other believers by giving gifts and making donations.

pages.title: Education in the Ahî Organization
pages.content:
Role models play an important part in Ahî education. They help people develop good behavior and learn a job. The Fütüvvetnâmeler clearly explain the qualities which these role models must have, such as performing the five daily prayers, staying modest, and avoiding selfish interests in this world. They must also stay away from what Allah has forbidden, obey His commands, earn a halal living, and generously support their brothers in faith. Finally, they must always encourage good deeds and prevent bad ones.

In general, seeking knowledge is a basic rule of the Ahî organization. Members should build close relations with scholars and ask for advice from experts. If a person does not have the skills needed for their job, they must learn them from a master or an educated person, and they must highly value that knowledge. According to traditional Ahî teachings, not learning a job properly brings shame both in this world and after death. Therefore, one must never try to do a job without correct training. As a result, the activities inside fütüvvet groups were in essence a form of education.

Young people who started Ahî training went through certain levels and tests. They started as apprentices, became experienced workers, and finally became masters. The goal of these steps was to help individuals use what they learned in their daily lives. In a way, every part of a zaviye member’s life was carefully watched. Through reading, talking, or following a role model, they learned the correct behavior for everyday situations, from walking on the street to visiting sick people.

Alongside madrasas (built in Anatolia after the arrival of the Turks) and Sufi tekkes that gave education to the public, Ahî zaviyes were also popular educational institutions with a very big impact. These zaviyes acted as schools and played a major role in educating the people of Anatolia. Their education covered all areas of life. These institutions shaped society’s worldview and served as cultural centers where Anatolian Turkish culture grew.

pages.title: The Ahîs and the Ottoman State
pages.content:
The Ahî movement also played a major role in the formation of the Ottoman Empire. Historical sources say that the Ahîs, who came from Turkmen groups, were one of the four main forces that helped build the empire. Some historians note that many of the early Ottoman sultans and viziers were connected with the Ahî organization. For example, Murad I joined this organization, and the group fought as soldiers during wars. However, especially starting in the rule of Mehmed II, the Ahî organization lost its political power. From that time on, it only managed the business affairs of artisan organizations.

In conclusion, the organization carried out important tasks not only in education but also in business, military, and political areas. Indeed, the 14th-century traveler from Tangier, Ibn Battuta, said that the Ahî organization was unique in the world. He noted that all the world’s beauties were found together in one place in Anatolia. The text attributes this to the brotherhood, which turned the region into a very rich area with great social, economic, and political order.

A person who makes things by hand.
The only one of its kind.
Says that something is caused by.

pages.title: Joining Ceremonies
pages.content:
Joining the Ahî organization included drinking şerbet, as well as wearing a traditional belt or peştamal and şalvar. These ceremonies had important meanings. For instance, wearing the traditional belt meant the following:

The belt has seven names, and each name carries one rule. The belt has seven rules. Tying and untying it carries seven distinct meanings. Each of these represents a different manner of behavior.

With the belt, doors are opened for good deeds and closed to bad ones, which welcomes good choices and rejects bad actions.

That is to say:

Close the door of stinginess and open the door of generosity,

Close the door of anger and open the door of patience,

Close the door of greed and open the door of being happy with what you have,

Close the door of worldly pleasures and open the door of self-discipline and repentance,

Close the door of expecting things from people and open the door of trusting the Creator,

Close the door of laziness and useless talk and open the door of knowledge and wisdom,

Close the door of bad choices and open the door of good actions.

transformItems.frame: People believe that his son [blank] him.

transformItems.source: Followers must avoid behaviors forbidden by the Qur’an.
transformItems.frame: Followers must stay away [blank] behaviors forbidden by the Qur’an.

exercises.explanation: “Act as” = “serve as”. A passive can become active. “Avoid” = “stay away from”.

feedback.correct: Well done. Same meaning, new structure.
feedback.incorrect: Use served, poisoned and from.

exercises.title: Use: A New Context
exercises.instructions: Read about a modern apprenticeship. Fill each gap from the word bank.
exercises.question: Can you use the book’s language in a new text?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Today, young carpenters are [blank] to train for three years. They learn [blank] working with a master. [blank] they finish, they get a certificate. The training is useful [blank] for work but also for life.
exercises.explanation: Be expected to, by + -ing and not only … but also come from the book. Here they describe a modern apprenticeship.

feedback.correct: Well done. You used the book’s language in a new text.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the words around each gap.

exercises.title: Use: Check a Short Report
exercises.instructions: A student wrote about a craft fair. Find and correct each mistake.
exercises.question: What should the student change?

errorItems.sentence: The masters, which came from many cities, showed their work.
Visitors must to pay a small fee.
The fair was not only fun but too useful.

exercises.explanation: Use who for people, must + base verb, and not only … but also.

feedback.correct: Correct. Who, must pay, but also.
feedback.incorrect: Check the relative pronoun, the modal and the pair.

exercises.title: Use: An Organization That Helps People
exercises.instructions: Write six to eight sentences about an organization that helps people today.
exercises.question: What does it do, and what rules do its members follow?
exercises.explanation: Example: “The Red Crescent in Türkiye started more than 150 years ago. It helps people after earthquakes, floods and wars. Volunteers are expected to be kind and patient. They must follow safety rules. The organization helps not only people in Türkiye but also people in other countries. Many young people join it to learn how to help. It is important because no one should be alone in a difficult time.”

feedback.correct: Check: are expected to, must, not only … but also and a clear reason.

discussionPrompts.question: Say what the organization is and when it started.
Describe two rules with are expected to and must.
Use not only … but also.
discussionPrompts.example: It helps not only … but also …

discussionPrompts.question: Say why it is important.

pages.title: Final Challenge
pages.content: Bring the whole book together in the Final Challenge.

exercises.title: Fütüvvet
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer that the book supports.
exercises.question: When did Fütüvvet start?
options: during the first century of Islam
during the rule of Mehmed II
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “Fütüvvet is a social concept that started during the first century of Islam.”

feedback.correct: Correct. The first century of Islam.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first sentence of Chapter 2.

exercises.title: People and Roles
exercises.instructions: Match each person with the right description.
exercises.question: Who was who in the book?

matchingPairs.right: the Abbasid Caliph who sent a Fütüvvet robe
the spiritual leader of leather workers
an Ottoman sultan who joined the organization

correctAnswer.Nâsır-Lidînillâh: the Abbasid Caliph who sent a Fütüvvet robe
correctAnswer.Ahî Evran: the spiritual leader of leather workers
correctAnswer.Murad I: an Ottoman sultan who joined the organization

exercises.explanation: Chapters 3, 4 and 7 introduce these four people.

feedback.correct: Correct. Each person matches a description.
feedback.incorrect: Look for each name in Chapters 3, 4 and 7.

exercises.title: Ahî Evran’s Zaviye
exercises.instructions: Complete the sentence from Chapter 4 with the name of a city.
exercises.question: Where did Ahî Evran found a zaviye?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Ahî Evran founded a zaviye in [blank] that became the socio-religious and professional center for artisans all across Anatolia.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4: “Known as the spiritual leader of leather workers and other craftsmen, Ahî Evran founded a zaviye in Kırşehir …”

feedback.correct: Correct. Kırşehir.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of the first paragraph of Chapter 4.

exercises.title: Business Duties
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer that the book supports.
exercises.question: Which were among the main duties of the organization?
options: checking the quality of goods and setting prices
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “Additionally, checking the quality of goods and setting the prices were among the main duties of the organization.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Quality and prices.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of the first paragraph of Chapter 5.

exercises.title: Close and Open
exercises.instructions: Match each door to close with the door to open.
exercises.question: What does the belt teach?

matchingPairs.right: being happy with what you have

correctAnswer.greed: being happy with what you have

exercises.explanation: Chapter 8 lists the seven doors of the belt.

feedback.correct: Correct. Each bad habit matches a good one.
feedback.incorrect: Read the list in Chapter 8.

exercises.title: The Four Main Forces
exercises.instructions: Read the statement. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: Historical sources say that the Ahîs were one of the four main forces that helped build the Ottoman Empire.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “Historical sources say that the Ahîs, who came from Turkmen groups, were one of the four main forces that helped build the empire.”

feedback.correct: Correct. One of four main forces.
feedback.incorrect: Read the beginning of Chapter 7.

exercises.title: The Caliph’s Plan
exercises.instructions: Read the statement. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: The Caliph wanted the Fütüvvet groups to stay independent of the state.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “As a result, this group, which was independent for a long time when central governments were weak, would now be under state control.”

feedback.correct: Correct. He wanted them under state control.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 3.

exercises.title: Levels of Training
exercises.instructions: Complete the sentence from Chapter 6 with one word.
exercises.question: What did apprentices finally become?
exercises.fillBlanksText: They started as apprentices, became experienced workers, and finally became [blank].
exercises.explanation: Chapter 6: “They started as apprentices, became experienced workers, and finally became masters.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Masters.
feedback.incorrect: Read the third paragraph of Chapter 6.

exercises.title: Ibn Battuta
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer that the book supports.
exercises.question: What did Ibn Battuta note about Anatolia?
options: All the world’s beauties were found together in one place there.
It was too cold to travel.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “He noted that all the world’s beauties were found together in one place in Anatolia.”

feedback.correct: Correct. All the world’s beauties in one place.
feedback.incorrect: Find Ibn Battuta in Chapter 7.

exercises.title: From Fütüvvet to the Ottomans
exercises.instructions: Put the events in the order they happened.
exercises.question: What happened first, next and last?

sequencingItems.text: Fütüvvet started during the first century of Islam.
The Caliph sent a Fütüvvet robe to Alâeddin Keykubad I.
The Ahîs helped defend Kayseri against the Mongols.
Murad I joined the Ahî organization.
The Ahî organization lost its political power under Mehmed II.

exercises.explanation: The book moves from the roots of Fütüvvet (Chapter 2) to the Seljuks (Chapters 3–4) and the Ottomans (Chapter 7).

feedback.correct: Correct. From Fütüvvet to the Ottomans.
feedback.incorrect: Think about the order of the chapters.
